headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Copilot can read repo/editor context while the prompt-list agent can shape instructions, creating unsafe default pairings.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a prompt/content-writing source that can supply arbitrary prompt text, while agent B ingests editor buffers and repo context by default. That creates a plausible instruction-injection path if A’s content is copied into B’s workspace or prompts. No shared channel is documented, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF content from agent A is pasted into agent B's chat or workspace context, injection is possible.
IF agent B treats copied prompt text as instructions rather than data, malicious directives can steer outputs.
mitigations: Keep agent A outputs out of agent B prompts unless manually sanitized.
Use a fixed delimiter/template when transferring text from A to B.
Review any A-generated prompt before pasting into B.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B reads filesystem content and repo context, and agent A is a content-writing prompt source with no stated isolation or data-handling controls. If sensitive code or secrets are present in B’s workspace, A can be exposed indirectly through copied context or shared files. The pair lacks documented shared-workspace isolation, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in agent B's repo context, they can be surfaced in outputs or copied into agent A prompts.
IF operators reuse the same workspace text between agents, data can cross from B to A.
mitigations: Exclude secrets from the repo context before using B.
Do not paste B outputs into A unless redacted.
Use separate workspaces for drafting and coding.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level redaction rules.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B can write files and modify git state, but agent A has no write or execution capabilities and is not runnable. That makes direct capability conflict limited; the main overlap is indirect through human-mediated content transfer, which is not a write-write race. I therefore keep this low.
conditions: IF agent A is manually used to generate patches that are then applied by agent B, conflicting edits can occur.
IF multiple B instances edit the same repo without coordination, git conflicts can arise.
mitigations: Use one editor session per branch.
Apply patches from A one at a time.
Run git status before accepting B edits.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared repos.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B’s Workspace/editing flow can turn upstream text into edits, and agent A produces prompt content that may be treated as authoritative by the operator. If A’s output is fed into B without verification, errors can cascade into code changes or commits. Because B proposes edits for review, not autonomous execution, medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF agent A-generated instructions are used as source material for B edits, mistakes can propagate into code changes.
IF the operator accepts B's proposed edits without review, downstream errors become persistent.
mitigations: Verify A-generated claims before using them in B.
Review every B patch before applying.
Keep a changelog of A-to-B transferred instructions.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking before edit generation.

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B is a closed-source GitHub Copilot service with vendor-only egress and GitHub repo context, while agent A is an open-source prompt list with no data classes touched. No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented in the profiles, so only a low compliance concern is supportable. I do not cite A for residency because none is stated.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into agent B's repo context, vendor-only egress may create a policy issue.
IF organizational policy forbids closed-source AI services for code context, deployment becomes noncompliant.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in B's context.
Check internal policy before enabling Copilot on sensitive repos.
Restrict B to non-sensitive repositories.
requires-engineering: document a data-processing agreement and retention review.
